title: Domain & Range, Composite, Inverse
videoTitle: Domain & Range, Composite, Inverse [IB Math AI HL]
intro: After this lesson you can evaluate a function, state its domain and range, build the composites $f\circ g$ and $g\circ f$, and find an inverse function, restricting the domain first when the function is not one-to-one.

moments.title: Three ways to write a function
moments.text: $f(x)=x^2-2$, $f: x\mapsto x^2-2$ and $y=x^2-2$ all describe the same rule. Use whichever your textbook uses.

moments.title: Evaluate by substitution
moments.text: $f(3)=7$, $g(-2)=1$ and $h(24)=5$. Find the function, then substitute the input for $x$.

moments.title: Domain and range
moments.text: The domain is the set of possible inputs ($x$ values). The range is the set of possible outputs ($y$ values).

moments.title: Domain and range of a quadratic
moments.text: $f(x)=x^2-2$ goes left and right forever, so $x\in\mathbb{R}$. It bottoms out at $-2$, so $y\ge-2$.

moments.title: A straight line
moments.text: $g(x)=x+3$ goes on forever in every direction, so both domain and range are all real numbers.

moments.title: A square root function
moments.text: $h(x)=\sqrt{x+1}$ starts at $x=-1$ and only gives non-negative outputs: domain $x\ge-1$, range $y\ge0$.

moments.title: A composite is a function of a function
moments.text: In $f\circ g$, the output of $g$ becomes the input of $f$.

moments.title: Find $f\circ g$
moments.text: Write $f$, and where it has $x$, put in $g(x)=x+3$. The result is $(x+3)^2-2$.

moments.title: Find $g\circ f$
moments.text: Start with $g$ and put $f(x)$ where $x$ was: $x^2-2+3=x^2+1$. A different order gives a different function.

moments.title: Inverse functions and their notation
moments.text: The inverse of $f$ is written $f^{-1}$. Start from $y=f(x)$.

moments.title: Swap $x$ and $y$, then solve for $y$
moments.text: The first step is always to swap $x$ and $y$. Then use algebra to make $y$ the subject.

moments.title: The inverse of $h$
moments.text: From $y=\sqrt{x+1}$: swap, square both sides, subtract 1. $h^{-1}(x)=x^2-1$.

moments.title: The inverse is a reflection
moments.text: The graph of $f^{-1}$ is the graph of $f$ reflected in the line $y=x$.

corrections.title: The video inverts $x^2-2$ without restricting the domain
corrections.text: It swaps and solves to get $\sqrt{x+2}$, but $f(x)=x^2-2$ on all real numbers is not one-to-one, so it has no inverse there.
corrections.write: $f(x)=x^2-2$ is not one-to-one on $\mathbb{R}$, so restrict to $x\ge0$ first. Then $f^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{x+2}$.

corrections.title: The video does not give the domain of an inverse
corrections.text: It finds $h^{-1}(x)=x^2-1$ but does not say where that function is defined.
corrections.write: $h^{-1}(x)=x^2-1$ for $x\ge0$, because the domain of $h^{-1}$ is the range of $h$.

sections.title: Does the function have an inverse?

cards.name: Test
cards.text: Does every output come from only one input? A horizontal line crosses the graph at most once.

cards.name: Restrict
cards.text: If not, keep one side of the turning point so the function is one-to-one.

cards.name: Swap and solve
cards.text: Write $y=f(x)$, swap $x$ and $y$, then solve for $y$.

cards.name: Domains swap
cards.text: The domain of $f^{-1}$ is the range of $f$. The range of $f^{-1}$ is the domain of $f$.

cells: None until the domain is restricted

notes.label: Wording check.
notes.text: The video finds $f^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{x+2}$ for $f(x)=x^2-2$ without restricting the domain first. A function needs an inverse to be one-to-one, so on an exam write $x\ge0$ before you swap. The syllabus lists domain restriction for inverse functions.

sections.title: Composite and inverse functions: the method
sections.intro: A composite function feeds the output of one function into another. An inverse undoes a function. Both come from substitution and rearranging.
steps: To find $(f\circ g)(x)=f(g(x))$, write $f$, then replace every $x$ in it with the whole expression for $g(x)$.
Simplify if the question asks. Check the order: $f\circ g$ and $g\circ f$ are usually different functions.
To find $f^{-1}$, first check that $f$ is one-to-one on its domain. If it is not, restrict the domain.
Write $y=f(x)$, swap $x$ and $y$, then solve for $y$. That $y$ is $f^{-1}(x)$.
State the domain of $f^{-1}$. It is the range of $f$.

parts.label: Composite: f then g
parts.text: With $f(x)=x^2-2$ and $g(x)=x+3$, replace the $x$ in $f$ with $x+3$. Expanded, $(f\circ g)(x)=x^2+6x+7$.

parts.label: Composite: g then f
parts.text: Start with $g$ and replace its $x$ with $x^2-2$: $(g\circ f)(x)=(x^2-2)+3=x^2+1$. A different order gives a different function.

parts.label: Inverse, with the restriction
parts.text: For $f(x)=x^2-2$ with $x\ge0$: write $y=x^2-2$, swap to $x=y^2-2$, so $y^2=x+2$ and $y=\sqrt{x+2}$ (positive root, because $y\ge0$). The domain is $x\ge-2$.

sections.title: Write it so it earns credit

traps.title: The order of a composite
traps.better: $(f\circ g)(x)=f(g(x))$, so $g$ acts first and then $f$. In practice, replace the $x$ in $f$ with $g(x)$.

traps.title: An inverse needs a restricted domain
traps.better: $f(x)=x^2-2$ is not one-to-one on $\mathbb{R}$, so restrict to $x\ge0$. Then $f^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{x+2}$ for $x\ge-2$.

traps.title: The inverse is not a reciprocal
traps.better: $f^{-1}$ is the inverse function, found by swapping $x$ and $y$. The reciprocal $\dfrac{1}{f(x)}$ is a different function.

traps.title: Include the end point of a domain
State the domain of the inverse
traps.better: $h^{-1}(x)=x^2-1$ for $x\ge0$, because the domain of $h^{-1}$ is the range of $h$.

sections.title: Write a full response
sections.prompt: The functions $f$ and $g$ are defined by $f(x)=(x+1)^2-3$ and $g(x)=2x-5$, for $x\in\mathbb{R}$.
sections.note: Give exact answers unless the question says otherwise. Show your working.
parts: (a) Find $(g\circ f)(x)$, giving your answer in the form $ax^2+bx+c$.
(b) Explain why $f$ has no inverse on $\mathbb{R}$, and give the largest domain of the form $x\ge k$ on which $f$ does have an inverse.
(c) For this restricted domain, find $f^{-1}(x)$ and state its domain.
sample: (b) $f(0)=f(-2)=-2$, so two different inputs give the same output. $f$ is not one-to-one, so it has no inverse on $\mathbb{R}$. The vertex is at $x=-1$, so $f$ is one-to-one for $x\ge-1$.
(c) Let $y=(x+1)^2-3$ and swap: $x=(y+1)^2-3$, so $(y+1)^2=x+3$. On $x\ge-1$ the inverse has $y\ge-1$, so $y+1=\sqrt{x+3}$ and $f^{-1}(x)=-1+\sqrt{x+3}$. The domain is $x\ge-3$, the range of $f$.
(d) $(f\circ g)(x)=(2x-5+1)^2-3=(2x-4)^2-3$. Setting this equal to 13 gives $(2x-4)^2=16$, so $2x-4=\pm4$ and $x=0$ or $x=4$.
checklist: (a) Puts $f(x)$ inside $g$, not the other way round, and simplifies to $2x^2+4x-9$.
(b) Gives two inputs with the same output (or uses the horizontal line test) and says $f$ is not one-to-one.
(c) Swaps $x$ and $y$, solves for $y$, and chooses the positive root because $y\ge-1$.
(c) States the domain $x\ge-3$ using the range of $f$.
(d) Puts $g$ inside $f$ and finds both solutions, $x=0$ and $x=4$.

flags.text: The video inverts f(x)=x^2-2 on all real numbers and gives sqrt(x+2) without saying f must be one-to-one first. The page adds the domain restriction (the syllabus lists it for AHL 2.7) and shows it in the decision table and a wording trap.
The video does not state the domain of an inverse function. The page adds that the domain of the inverse is the range of the original (rows and traps for f and h).

Syllabus codes SL 2.2 and AHL 2.7. The video covers function notation, domain and range (SL 2.2) as well as composite and inverse functions (AHL 2.7). The identity (f o f^-1)(x)=x and the rows for g, p, and the x<=0 branch of f are not in the video; they come from the syllabus guidance.

Captions at about 0:45 ('a little pole in here as X with a little arrow') mean the maps-to notation f: x -> x^2-2, and at 2:10 ('my is positive one') means 'my output is 1'. Notation was rebuilt from context.
Every value on the page was computed and checked with sympy. Domain and range statements and the inverse domains were worked out from the function definitions, not read off graphs.
No GDC section: no emulator captures exist yet for this topic. The video suggests graphing h on a calculator (about 6:15), which would suit a later GDC section.
Decision rows for g, p and the x<=0 branch have no video link because the video does not cover them.
